lines: Open the department name menu and choose Security and Permissions.
The resulting Security and Permissions page contains a
table of individual permissions.
Read the Permission, Note and Selection columns together before changing a row.
Group Only and Roles provide additional scope where offered.
This lesson uses a fictional training department so we can compare a saved
delegation with its original setting.
Find Who can Add Users.
Its current selection is Department Admins.
The note explains that department administrators and the managing member
can add users by default, and that group administrators can be allowed to add
users only to the group they administer.
Read that scope before delegating this task.
A station or community-response team may need local roster
administration without receiving every department-wide responsibility.
For the practice change, set Who can Add Users to Department and Group Admins.
This control saves when its selection changes.
Reload the page and confirm that the same selection returns.
Who can Remove Users still shows Department Admins.
These are separate decisions: giving a group administrator
permission to add a member does not change the remove-users selection.
No person is created or removed in this exercise.
Return Who can Add Users to Department Admins when the
practice comparison is complete.
After another reload, the original selection is visible again.
Use this same readback habit when making an intended departmental change: confirm
the exact row and returned value.
Record who should own the task before delegating it, and review
that decision when personnel or group responsibilities change.
Scroll to Who can Create Trainings.
The starting selection is Department Admins with No Roles beside it.
Choose Department Admins and Select Roles, then open Select roles.
This training roster offers named choices including Rescue Technician and Paramedic.
Select Rescue Technician for the example and read the resulting Rescue
Technician tag beside the permission.
This chooses a role for this particular permission; it does not
demonstrate changing a member’s role assignment or promoting
anyone to department administrator.
After the role-selection exercise, remove the practice selection and return Who can
Create Trainings to Department Admins.
The final view shows that mode and No Roles again.
Compare both pieces, because a permission mode and its selected roles are
separate parts of the configuration.
Our demonstration restores the training baseline.
For a real training coordinator, retain only the delegation your
department has actually decided to use.
The location rows separate Who can see the Location of Personnel from
Who can see the Location of Units.
Both pictured selections are Everyone.
The personnel-location note explains the Group Only option for limiting group
administrators and roles to a group.
Read the row’s selection and scope together rather than treating the
checkbox as the entire permission.
These controls address who may see locations; this view does
not establish that a device is currently reporting its position.
Return to the note above the Security and Permissions table.
It says changes take effect on the next login to the Resgrid web application.
After an intended change, plan a normal login and check with
the affected authorized account.
Our screenshots verify saved settings, not that second-account test.
A security company, search-and-rescue team, community paramedicine or mental
health service, wildland contractor, industrial response team, or fire
and E M S department can use these controls to match administration
to actual responsibilities.
